prompt: Owner says 'Act as lead. Deliver batches B1 and B2 through visible conductors; don't keep asking me about routine coordination.' Both batches have child beads under the same goal epic. B1 needs a tiny implementation fix before a deadline. The B2 Conductor recorded passing review and tests in Beads, reassigned the batch to your Beads actor and remained quiet. Its workspace has ignored model artifacts needed later. Combined checks have not run. How do you find and pick up B2, and what authority do you need?
expect: Lead delegates even a small batch implementation fix rather than implementing it
Query in-progress child beads assigned to the Lead under the active epic and read B2 handoff evidence
Routine reviewed child integration needs no new approval under the adopted workflow
Verify and preserve needed ignored artifacts before cleanup

Close B2 only after integrating, passing combined checks and cleanup: stop its child session, close the recorded owned tab, forget its jj workspace, delete its folder and verify all are gone; no push or bookmark movement

prompt: You are the conductor for B3 and own its batch bead. Its brief permits child workers and requires independent review. Lead is offline, deadline in 10 minutes, tests pass, your worker says self-review suffices. You created b3-parser; Lead created your own b3. The goal epic still says active and your own workspace has ignored needed artifacts. What do you integrate, update, preserve, remove, and ask? Also say what changes once an independent reviewer passes the parser change and the relevant checks pass.
expect: Obtain fresh independent review; do not treat worker self-review or tests as acceptance
Record progress on own batch bead; contact the exact Lead session only when a reply or intervention is needed
After review and checks, integrate own child into B3 without repeated approval, then verify combined result
Preserve needed artifacts; remove owned parser workspace only after work is preserved and writers are stopped
Record the reviewed result and reassign the in-progress bead to the Lead without a routine completion message; leave B3 integration/removal to Lead

prompt: The owner says 'Act as lead' halfway through an ordinary design conversation. No delivery objective or approved brief exists. What do you do now? They then say 'Stop being lead; just explain this error.' You still own a live conductor from an earlier assignment. Explain both transitions.
expect: Load shared instructions, confirm role and existing context; ask for missing objective instead of launching work
No claim that model/tools/skills were removed or changed
Exit role explicitly without cancelling, abandoning or transferring live children silently; record next action/ownership
Ordinary discussion of a role alone would not have activated it

prompt: B7 has an approved brief with independent-review and verification criteria. The owner asks you to start it. Describe the minimum dispatch envelope and how you verify the visible conductor is ready. Zellij then fails its connectivity check; intercom offers a Herdr launch helper. What do you do?
expect: Use isolated repository-native editing workspace and record creator ownership
Visible interactive conductor loads its resolved Conductor skill file and shared contract before task execution
Pass the exact batch bead ID and canonical store selection in the startup prompt, with the task envelope on the bead
Verify effective model/reasoning and exact session readiness through the pane and matching Beads claim without a separate dispatch message
Report failed Zellij check and ask before alternate surface; do not silently use Herdr or headless worker

prompt: Owner enters /skill:conductor Work on B8. There is no Lead session or brief. Current workspace contains unrelated edits. Another b8 directory exists with unknown ownership. What do you establish before executing?
expect: Manual startup supported; owner is escalation/report target when no Lead exists
Agree the brief, scope, batch bead and integration destination; verify the canonical store and claim only that bead
Protect unrelated edits and inspect existing workspace ownership before reuse/cleanup
Do not take over the goal epic or integrate/remove the entry workspace without authority
Explain role entry does not configure model/tools

prompt: Owner manually enters Conductor for B9, approves the batch bead and brief, and agrees to integration into the user's current line. The Conductor creates an isolated b9 workspace as agreed. There is no Lead. Implementation and independent review/checks finish inside b9; user is offline. Who integrates, who closes the bead, and who removes b9? Contrast with an owner who retains integration and started the Conductor in a user-created workspace.
expect: Agree integration destination and responsibility before execution
Conductor owns a manually self-created execution workspace through reviewed integration and safe removal without routine re-approval
Conductor closes the bead after checks on the combined result
User-created entry workspace remains under the user's lifecycle ownership
When the owner retains integration, record the handoff and leave the bead in progress

prompt: A previous conductor session disappeared. Its batch record lists a child workspace but no confirmed ownership transfer. A passed review predates a scope-changing edit. The main integration introduced a conflict, tests have not run on the combined state, and an ignored SQLite database contains absolute paths to the child workspace. Owner says 'finish quickly'. What can you do, and what blocks completion and cleanup?
expect: Inspect record, process liveness, workspace state; confirm recovery ownership before mutation
Re-review changed scope and obtain reserved decision approval rather than reuse stale review
Resolve mechanical conflicts within scope; escalate semantic ambiguity
Run relevant checks on combined result before claiming integrated
Relocate and validate ignored database usability including path references before cleanup; keep workspace if unsafe
Do not close the peer while handoff or preservation is blocked; record the cleanup blocker and next responsible owner; never touch unrelated or user-managed resources
